card.name: First digit of a dose number
card.fires_on: The first digit (or the space before it) of a number in a dose, weight or volume, such as the 4 in 45 or the 5 in 0.5 mL. Mostly in dosing text with mg, kg or mL.

modes.label: Digit after decimal point
modes.description: A digit right after "0." in a dose or volume amount.
modes.example: HBsAg-positive should receive 0.<<5>> mL Hepatitis B Immune Globulin

modes.label: Leading digit of a dose or formula
modes.description: The first digit of a whole number in a dosing regimen or weight formula.
modes.example: = 50 + 0.91 x (height in cm - 152) Women: IBW (kg) = <<4>>5 + 0.91 x

modes.label: Space before a number
modes.description: The space just before a large amount in general text.
modes.example: They will share half the prize of<< >>1.4 million dollars, the other

card.writes: It pushes against value and currency words, so the number is not read as money or worth.
card.plain: It marks the start of a dose number, such as 0.5 mL or 45 kg, and not a money amount.
